t: The dynasty that overthrew the Shang in 1046 BCE and ruled northern China from Haojing near modern Xi'an.
It proclaimed the Mandate of Heaven: Heaven grants rule to the virtuous and withdraws it from the wicked.
It governed through regional states held by royal kinsmen, which later grew into the rival powers of the Warring States.
dyk: The He zun, a bronze vessel cast under King Cheng, contains the earliest known use of zhongguo, 'the central state', later the Chinese name for China.
ev: King Wu defeats the Shang at the Battle of Muye
The Duke of Zhou crushes the Rebellion of the Three Guards
King Zhao dies on a disastrous southern campaign
King Li is driven out and the Gonghe regency begins
King Xuan begins a revival against the Xianyun and the Huaiyi
The Quanrong and the Marquis of Shen sack Haojing and kill King You

f.capital: Feng and Haojing; eastern capital at Chengzhou (Luoyi)
